subject: specifying Nsize and offset with prediction stacks

messages.author: 58acd2f2d6929a53
messages.subject: specifying Nsize and offset with prediction stacks
parts:
I am trying to do a spatial (actually 1D) model which has a similar structure to what is described in "Advanced Spatial Modeling with Stochastic Partial Differential Equations Using R and INLA" in Chapter 3.1 (coregionalization).  Differences of my situation are that I have not 3 but 2 likelihoods (that is obviously minor) and that one is gaussian and the other binomial (that is what causes me problems syntactically), plus I do have either a covariate and/or offset for the binomial part.

 

I have no problem to fit the model, estimate beta coefficients etc. But what I need to get is to  get predictions at new locations, for new covariate values etc. To this end, I do something like:

…

spde1.idx <- inla.spde.make.index("s12", n.spde = spde$n.spde)

stack1 <- inla.stack(

  data = list(y = cbind(as.vector(pom[,1]), NA)),

  A = list(1,A1),

 effects = list(list(I1=rep(1,nrow(pom)),recoat= c(pom1[,"Recoated.m"],pom2[,"PIPE_LENGTH"]) ),spde1.idx),tag="est1" )

 

#

spde2.idx <- inla.spde.make.index("s2", n.spde = spde$n.spde)

stack2 <- inla.stack(

  data = list(y = cbind(NA,as.vector(pom[,2]))),

  A = list(1,A1),

  effects = list(list(I2= rep(1,nrow(pom))), spde2.idx),tag="est2")

#

# Predict at original positions
xx1 <- c(pom1$ABS_POS,pom2$ABS_POS)

## extend est position by one !!!

#xx1 <- c(pom1$ABS_POS,pom2$ABS_POS,10)

n.xx1<-length(xx1)

A.xx1 <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh1d, xx1)

#

stack.pred1<-inla.stack(

  data = list(y = cbind(rep(NA,n.xx1), NA)),

  A = list(1,A.xx1),

  effects = list(list(I1=rep(1,n.xx1),recoat=rep(12,n.xx1)),spde1.idx),tag="pred1" )

#

stack.pred2<-inla.stack(

  data = list(y = cbind(NA, rep(NA,n.xx1))),

  A = list(1,A.xx1),

  effects = list(list(I2=rep(1,n.xx1)),spde2.idx),tag="pred2" )

#

stack<-inla.stack(stack1,stack2,stack.pred1,stack.pred2)

#

bivspat.spde.cor.reg <- inla(y ~ 0 +I1+I2+f(s12, copy="s2", fixed=FALSE)+ f(s2, model = spde)+recoat, data = inla.stack.data(stack),

  control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack),compute=TRUE),

  control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE,waic=TRUE),control.fixed=list(correlation.matrix=TRUE),

  family = c("binomial", "gaussian"),Ntrials=rep(1,nrow(pom)))

  

 

This seems to work fine as long as I actually do the prediction (pred1, pred2) at the original locations (which obviously has no point except for checking), or as long as the number of pred locations is the same as est locations.

Apparently, the problem is in the Ntrials argument. Even when it is uniformly 1, I do not know how to specify the correct length vector size (do not know what its size should be if I have the additional pred1, pred2 stacks).

If I extend the pred stacks by one and leave Ntrials at the value I used just for the estimation (without the pred stacks), I get the error:
 Error in data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE) :

  arguments imply differing number of rows: 1962, 490

 

Even though I realized that I can get the code running by using Nsize=rep(1,1962) after seeing the message, I feel uneasy since I do not understand how the 1962 is constructed (does not seem to be a simple multiple/sum of what I have for est and pred).
 Obviously, the problem would be exposed even more explicitly if the Nsize would not be uniform – I have no idea how to enter the vector.

 

I think that I would be faced with the similar problem if I would like specify offset (as a separate argument, not within the linear predictor) in this situation.


How to go about it systematically? That is, how do I know number and ordering of Nsize and offset that is needed for a given model with complicated stacks and more than one likelihood?

All the Best

 Marek

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] specifying Nsize and offset with prediction stacks
parts:
Hi,

for data-length vectors, you can add them to the data part of the
stacks, and extract them when needed:

s1 <- inla.stack(data=list(y =..., Ntrials =...),...)
s2 <- inla.stack(data=list(y =..., Ntrials =...),...)
s <- inla.stack(s1,s2)
s_data <- inla.stack.data(s)
inla(..., data = s_data, Ntrials <- s_data$Ntrials, ...)

It should work similarly for offsets.

Finn
